label: early original-phase step (t=2-3) after a prefix of t/v/x/y/c/3/e/q, current token x/c/3/q/l/v/o/a/g/i
explanation: Fires only in the original phase at steps t=2-5 (about 89% of mass at t=2-3, ~11% at t=4, almost none at t=5); never fires at t=0-1, on the delimiter, or during copy. Within that window it acts like an additive token-identity score. It is strongest when the first two inputs come from {t,v,x,y,c,3,e,q} and the current input is from {x,c,3,q,l,...}; the top examples are prefixes like t v x x, v y x x, e x t x. It favors first occurrences of a token (in_first share 83%). Magnitude rises with how many favored tokens are in the prefix and whether the current token is favored. Activation is weak or missing when the prefix has other letters. The boolean predicate only approximates this graded token-weighting (dev F1 0.54, precision 0.71, mass recall 0.62), so it is partially explained.
